clue.text: Damage from use found in Excalibur is profanity

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other, so it sits within the sword's letters

parts.note: Excalibur is King Arthur's sword
wear is the damage caused by use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that misusing the legendary blade has made it a vulgar thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A profanity is an oath or obscene utterance, which is exactly what a curse word is.

clue.text: Man's doctor in error

parts.note: the S from the possessive is used as a letter

indicators.note: in error suggests the letters are muddled and must be put right

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's physician has made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder, not part of the indicator: 'error' alone scrambles S, MO and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon is a man's name, so the answer is an example of a man.

clue.text: French rulers no longer in such numbers?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in office
the Directory governed revolutionary France from 1795 to 1799

explanation.surface: A question about phone numbers for those who once governed France.
explanation.walkthrough: Ex-directory is British for an unlisted telephone number, one left out of the phone book.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers withheld from the telephone directory are called ex-directory in Britain.

clue.text: Holder of crown putting brake on progress

definitions.text: Holder of crown putting brake on progress

parts.words: Holder of crown putting brake on progress
parts.note: the crown is the raised middle of a road; a driver who hogs it holds up other traffic

explanation.surface: A monarch is accused of holding back reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' suggests a king, but it is the centre of the road, where a selfish motorist stays and slows everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish driver who takes up the middle of the road obstructs others' progress.

clue.text: In river abroad, tend shrub

indicators.note: In places the inclining word inside the foreign river

parts.note: the Oder is a river in central Europe
to lean is to tend or incline

explanation.surface: Someone abroad looks after a bush beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen flowering bush, a common ornamental shrub.

clue.text: Persistent old magistrate arrests grand duke

indicators.note: arrests means holds, so the magistrate takes the grand letter inside

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice and Genoa
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A tenacious former judge detains a high-ranking nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged means stubbornly determined, which is a synonym of persistent.

clue.text: Set time kept by composer

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the time letter goes within the composer

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer

explanation.surface: A composer holds on to a fixed tempo throughout a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A set and a batch are both a group of things made or taken together.

clue.text: Garment a party held very daring

indicators.note: held means the others keep the very letter between them

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A risqué outfit worn at a party was thought very bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness, a noun for daring display.

clue.text: Disapproving expression as skirt is shortened

indicators.note: is shortened means the skirt word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tutu is a ballet skirt

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at how short a skirt has become.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is an exclamation of disapproval or impatience.

clue.text: Like a large piece? Fish is excellent

parts.note: a hunk is a large piece, so hunky jokingly means like one
the dory is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a chunky fillet of fish is any good.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine, satisfactory, all going well.

clue.text: Sorceress giving me term of affection? That's not right

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not right asks for the letter R, the abbreviation for right, to be dropped

parts.note: dear is an affectionate form of address

explanation.surface: Someone is called 'dear' by a witch and objects that it is inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: Medea is the sorceress of Greek myth who helped Jason win the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Medea is the enchantress of Greek legend, a classic example of a sorceress.

clue.text: Side a bit short, originally bringing half a team to ground

indicators.note: a bit short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: an edge is a side or border

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word
half asks for only one of the two words of the team's name

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club

explanation.surface: A cricket side, slightly under strength, brings half its players to the field.
explanation.walkthrough: EDGBASTON is the Test cricket ground in Birmingham; ASTON is the first of the two words of Aston Villa, another Birmingham sporting name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgbaston is a famous English cricket venue, so it is an example of a sports ground.

clue.text: Novel point — cloistered house conceals passion

indicators.note: conceals means the first pieces hide the last one between them

parts.note: north is a point of the compass
an abbey is a monastic house with cloisters
anger is a passion or strong emotion

explanation.surface: A tale in which a monastery hides a fierce emotion behind its walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Jane Austen's Gothic satire, set partly in Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Northanger Abbey is a Jane Austen book, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Rolls acquired by this traditional husband?

definitions.text: Rolls acquired by this traditional husband?

parts.words: Rolls acquired by this traditional husband?
parts.note: rolls are bread, which the traditional working husband wins, slang for earning money

explanation.surface: A question about a husband who buys bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so the earner is the one bringing it home.
explanation.definitionFit: The family's main earner wins the bread, the money, as the husband traditionally did.

clue.text: On track, perhaps better drivers extremely eager to contain selfishness

indicators.note: to contain means the other pieces surround the selfishness word

parts.note: the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is the British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of the next word

parts.note: ego is self-regard or selfishness

explanation.surface: Motorists, keen to the limit, are told to keep their egotism in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is someone who bets, not 'superior'; 'On track, perhaps' says the bet is placed at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A person attending race meetings often places wagers there, so a punter at the track fits.

clue.text: Hall, one element in professional house

indicators.note: in places the element symbol inside the house

parts.note: a rectory is the house that goes with a rector's professional post
Fe is the chemical symbol of iron, one element

explanation.surface: A building where a single component sits in a business premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is a dining hall in a monastery or college.

clue.text: Craftily stopped having to go to seaside town

indicators.note: go to means the short word is placed after the town

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town on the Sussex coast, next to Brighton
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly halted because they had to travel to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craftily' points to a craft, a boat: to heave to is to bring a vessel to a stop, and its past tense is hove to.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove to is the nautical past tense for bringing a sailing vessel to a standstill.

clue.text: The virtue of operetta

definitions.meaning: the quality of waiting calmly, proverbially a virtue
the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera that satirises aesthetes

explanation.surface: A claim that a light opera embodies a particular moral quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a virtue, and also the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.

clue.text: Potter's lot failing to break Voldemort, say

indicators.note: to break means the scrambled letters split the enemy word open

parts.note: Voldemort is Harry Potter's arch-enemy, an example of a foe

indicators.note: failing signals the word lot is broken down and rearranged

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's friends fail to defeat the Dark Lord.
explanation.walkthrough: Voldemort pulls the reader towards Harry Potter, but 'Potter' is the verb, to dawdle or fiddle about aimlessly; 'failing' makes OTL from LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To footle is to mess about idly, a synonym of potter about.

clue.text: In stories, child uses a figure of speech

indicators.note: In puts the little one inside the stories word

parts.note: stories can mean lies, fibs
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster uses rhetorical devices in their tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, a rhetorical figure.

clue.text: Gradually, or through a series of revolutions?

definitions.meaning: little by little, a step at a time
each day is one rotation of the Earth, so a succession of turns of the planet

explanation.surface: Change comes slowly, or else through one uprising after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means progressively, and literally a run of days is a run of Earth's rotations.

clue.text: Victorian author's book, mature and passionate

parts.note: to age is to mature
hot means passionate

explanation.surface: A book by a nineteenth-century writer is both seasoned and steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Bagehot wrote The English Constitution and edited The Economist.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Bagehot was a nineteenth-century essayist and economist, so a Victorian writer.

clue.text: Records regular books not acceptable

indicators.note: not asks for the acceptable letter to be left out

parts.note: annuals are books published every year
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Accounts of repeated volumes are deemed unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are year-by-year historical records.

clue.text: As sole agent, make self-defeatingly high claims

definitions.text: As sole agent, make self-defeatingly high claims

parts.words: As sole agent, make self-defeatingly high claims
parts.note: a sole is a fish; a fish selling itself by claiming to be high, meaning smelly and off, runs down its own goods

explanation.surface: An exclusive salesman talks up his product so much that he undermines it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole agent' reads as an exclusive seller, but sole is the fish, and 'high' means rotten-smelling rather than lofty.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage one's own wares or efforts is the idiom's meaning, crying that one's fish is rotten.

clue.text: Keep host talking

indicators.note: talking means the word is as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a host is a great multitude, a horde

explanation.surface: A party host is told to keep the conversation going.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to keep or store away a stock of something.

clue.text: Run past peak, perhaps, in bad weather on plain

indicators.note: in a down-style charade, on here means the weather follows the first piece

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: An athlete runs past a summit in a downpour on flat ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peak' is a fitness peak, not a mountain: to overtrain is to keep training beyond the best condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to exercise excessively so that performance falls off past its best.

clue.text: Part of crop needs attention

definitions.meaning: the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant such as corn

explanation.surface: A farmer says part of the harvest needs looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is the grain head of wheat, and giving an ear means paying attention.

clue.text: Hard to recall girl's colouring

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to remember a woman's hair dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye from a plant, used to colour hair and skin.

clue.text: Germany pressed quite a bit here

definitions.text: Germany pressed quite a bit here

indicators.note: quite a bit means a sizeable part of the words, the answer sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A war memory: the German army pushed hard at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The town in Flanders was the site of several German offensives in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres in Belgium is where German forces mounted repeated attacks during the Great War.

clue.text: Her eldest, defective, in such accommodation?

indicators.note: defective suggests the letters of the words are faulty and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A mother's oldest child, now frail, lives in housing for those needing care.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheltered accommodation is British housing for older or disabled people with a warden on call.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered housing is supervised accommodation for the elderly, the kind the frail eldest might live in.
